item.skill_text: Design for vector data, including vector data type, vector indexes, and size
item.stem: A product team is adding semantic search over support articles in Azure SQL Database. They will store one embedding per article, produced by a new model that returns 3,072 numeric values for each article. Queries must find the nearest articles by similarity, not filter or join on exact vector values. They ask you to design the table column and indexing approach and explain any size-related choices. What would you do and why?

rubric.point: Chooses a VECTOR column whose dimension count matches the embedding and explicitly uses float16 because 3,072 dimensions fit float16 but exceed float32 capacity.
rubric.quote: float32 supports up to 1,998 dimensions. float16 supports up to 3,996 dimensions.

rubric.point: States that relying on the default base type would select float32, so the column definition must name float16 explicitly.
rubric.quote: If you don't specify a base type, the vector uses float32.

rubric.point: Uses a vector index on the vector column for nearest-neighbor similarity search and describes it as approximate search for performance.
rubric.quote: Vector indexes create an approximate index on a vector column to improve the performance of nearest neighbors search.

rubric.point: Chooses the supported vector-indexing approach and says B-tree or columnstore indexes are unavailable for indexing vector columns directly.
rubric.quote: You can't use B-tree indexes or columnstore indexes on vector columns.

item.model_answer: I would store each article embedding in a column such as Embedding VECTOR(3072, float16), with NOT NULL if every article must have an embedding. I would not use VECTOR(3072) without a base type, because that defaults to float32, and float32 supports fewer dimensions than the 3,072 values returned by this model. In Azure SQL Database, float16 is the right size choice for this dimension count. For search performance, I would create a vector index on the embedding column for approximate nearest-neighbor similarity search. I would keep normal keys and metadata in separate relational columns and not try to use a B-tree or columnstore index directly on the vector column.

answers.text: I'd add a column Embedding VECTOR(3072, float16) NOT NULL. The base type has to be written out: if I just wrote VECTOR(3072), SQL would use the default float32, and float32 vectors can't hold 3,072 dimensions, while float16 can. For the nearest-article queries I'd create a vector index on Embedding and query it with approximate nearest-neighbour search, trading a little exactness for speed. A regular B-tree or columnstore index can't be put on a vector column, so the vector index is the only way to index it.
Store it as VECTOR(3072) and keep the default float32 for full precision; add a nonclustered B-tree index on the vector column so similarity lookups are fast.
Use a VECTOR(3072, float16) column, because with 3,072 values float32 would be over its dimension limit. I'd query it with VECTOR_DISTANCE and ORDER BY to get the top articles.

- column: Embedding vector(3072, float16)
- float16 because float32 maxes out below 3072 dims
- vector(3072) alone = float32 default -> must say float16
- vector index (approximate nearest neighbor) on Embedding
- no btree / columnstore on vector columns
